questions.title: False statement about viral conjunctivitis
questions.question: In viral conjunctivitis, all of the following are true, EXCEPT:

options.A: It is self-limiting, resolving in about 14 days
options.B: It is characterised by enlarged tender pre-auricular lymph nodes
options.D: It is one of the causes of follicular conjunctivitis

explanations.A: Incorrect (a true statement). Viral (adenoviral) conjunctivitis is self-limiting and resolves over about two weeks.
explanations.B: Incorrect (a true statement). A tender enlarged preauricular lymph node is characteristic of viral conjunctivitis.
explanations.C: Correct. This is the false statement: viral conjunctivitis is highly CONTAGIOUS, spreading readily by contact and causing epidemics, so calling it non-contagious is wrong. The other statements are all true of it. Its contagiousness is exactly why hand hygiene and isolation are advised.
explanations.D: Incorrect (a true statement). Viral conjunctivitis produces a follicular conjunctival reaction.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise that viral conjunctivitis is contagious, not non-contagious.

questions.title: Contraindicated drop in acute anterior uveitis
questions.question: A 37-year-old man presents with aching pain and blurred vision in the left eye for 5 days. Slit-lamp examination shows fine keratic precipitates, aqueous cells and flare. Which of the following medications is CONTRAINDICATED?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Topical corticosteroids are a mainstay of treating anterior uveitis, to suppress the inflammation.
explanations.B: Correct. Pilocarpine, a miotic, is contraindicated in acute anterior uveitis: constricting the inflamed pupil promotes posterior synechiae and worsens pain and inflammation. The pupil should instead be dilated with a cycloplegic such as atropine to rest the ciliary body and prevent synechiae. So the miotic is the contraindicated drop.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Atropine, a cycloplegic, is exactly what is indicated to dilate the pupil and prevent synechiae.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Timolol may be added if the pressure rises, and is not contraindicated.

questions.learning_objective: Identify miotics as contraindicated in acute anterior uveitis, where a cycloplegic is used.

questions.title: Complication of trachoma
questions.question: Complications of trachoma include:

explanations.A: Incorrect. A descemetocele is a complication of a deep corneal ulcer, not of trachoma.
explanations.B: Correct. Trachoma scars the upper tarsal conjunctiva, and the contracting scar rolls the lid margin inward as a cicatricial entropion with trichiasis. The inturned lashes abrade and scar the cornea and can blind the eye. So cicatricial entropion is a classic trachoma complication.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Subconjunctival haemorrhage is unrelated to trachoma.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Trachoma causes cicatricial entropion rather than ptosis.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise cicatricial entropion with trichiasis as a complication of trachoma.

questions.title: Disease that does not present with panuveitis
questions.question: Panuveitis is a common presentation in the following diseases, EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect (it causes panuveitis). Behcet disease classically causes a panuveitis with hypopyon.
explanations.B: Correct. Rheumatoid arthritis is the exception: its ocular disease is scleritis and keratoconjunctivitis sicca (dry eye), not panuveitis. Behcet, VKH and sarcoidosis are the systemic causes of panuveitis. So rheumatoid arthritis does not present as panuveitis.
explanations.C: Incorrect (it causes panuveitis). Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada syndrome is a bilateral granulomatous panuveitis.
explanations.D: Incorrect (it causes panuveitis). Sarcoidosis is a classic cause of granulomatous panuveitis.

questions.learning_objective: Separate the systemic causes of panuveitis from rheumatoid arthritis.

questions.title: Danger of topical steroids in a viral corneal ulcer
questions.question: Topical steroids are contraindicated in a case of viral corneal ulcer for fear of:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Secondary uveitis is not the feared consequence of steroids in a herpetic ulcer.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cataract is a long-term steroid effect, not the acute danger in a viral ulcer.
explanations.C: Correct. Topical steroids in a viral (herpes simplex) corneal ulcer suppress local immunity, allowing the dendritic ulcer to enlarge into a geographic ulcer and to deepen with stromal melting toward corneal perforation. This is the feared complication. So steroids are withheld for fear of perforation.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Some scarring may occur, but the dangerous acute risk driving the contraindication is perforation.

questions.learning_objective: Explain that topical steroids in a viral corneal ulcer risk corneal perforation.

questions.title: True statement about herpes simplex keratitis
questions.question: As regards herpes simplex, which statement is true?

options.A: It typically shows as an epithelial dendritic ulcer
options.C: It is mainly treated by topical antibiotics
options.D: It is never a recurrent problem

explanations.A: Correct. Herpes simplex keratitis typically presents as a branching epithelial dendritic ulcer that stains with fluorescein. It is treated with topical antivirals such as acyclovir, and it is characteristically recurrent. So the dendritic ulcer is its typical presentation.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Herpes simplex keratitis does not cause retinal detachment.
explanations.C: Incorrect. It is treated with a topical antiviral, not antibiotics.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Herpes simplex keratitis is characteristically a recurrent disease.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise the dendritic epithelial ulcer as the typical presentation of herpes simplex keratitis.

questions.title: Best vital stain for a corneal ulcer
questions.question: The best vital stain to detect a corneal ulcer is:

explanations.A: Correct. Fluorescein is the best vital stain to detect a corneal ulcer: it pools in and stains areas of denuded epithelium bright green under cobalt-blue light, outlining the ulcer and its dendritic or geographic shape. It is the standard bedside stain for an epithelial defect. So fluorescein is the answer.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Rose Bengal stains devitalised cells and mucus (useful in dry eye), not the first choice for an ulcer.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Trypan blue is used to stain the anterior capsule during cataract surgery, not to detect an ulcer.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Lissamine green stains devitalised cells like Rose Bengal, not the ulcer bed.

questions.learning_objective: Select fluorescein as the vital stain used to detect a corneal ulcer.

questions.title: Correct treatment of a corneal ulcer
questions.question: A corneal ulcer should be treated as follows:

options.A: Topical antimicrobial eye drops, cycloplegia, eye patching
options.B: Topical antimicrobial eye drops, cycloplegia, no eye patching
options.D: Oral antibiotics, cycloplegia, no eye patching

explanations.A: Incorrect. The correct treatment uses topical drops but the eye must NOT be patched.
explanations.B: Correct. An infective corneal ulcer is treated with intensive topical antimicrobial drops and a cycloplegic for comfort and to prevent synechiae, and the eye is NOT patched. Patching creates a warm moist closed space that encourages microbial growth and can worsen the infection. So topical antimicrobials, cycloplegia and no patch is correct.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Treatment is by topical, not oral, antimicrobials, and the eye is not patched.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The mainstay is topical antimicrobials rather than oral antibiotics.

questions.learning_objective: State that an infective corneal ulcer is treated with topical antimicrobials and cycloplegia, without patching.
